meta.workflow_angle: Verification-method improvements: information monotonicity, robust verdicts under tolerance, verified explanations, verified scheduling.
meta.method: Read README.md, VERIFICATION_SCOPE.md, paper.md, lean/CryoLean/*.lean (Checker, Spec, Model, Num, Schedule, Explain, and the newly added Monotone.lean), data/physics, data/experiments, data/cryostats and paper/data. Re-ran the compiled Lean checker read-only on all 286 pairs against a copy of data/cryolean.db in the session scratchpad; the 20 / 109 / 157 counts were reproduced exactly, and all derived numbers come from that run. Literature and sources were retrieved with Tavily (search, extract), WebSearch, WebFetch, the built-in browser (Lake Shore CCS-100 page), Lune (search_papers_many, search_papers, get_paper_fulltext, verify_claims), alphaXiv (discover_papers, answer_pdf_queries), Consensus (search) and Undermind (search_papers, get_paper_info). scite was not usable: its MCP tools require a paid plan.

The proposals build on them. Sibling workflow outputs in this folder (thermal.json TH3/TH4, magnet.json MAG-1/MAG-4, requirements.json R5) were read to avoid duplication and are cross-referenced.

proposals.title: Pipeline-wide information monotonicity: extend verdict_refines to experiment parameters, a Lean-side cooling-power bracket, duplicate keys and schedules
proposals.description:
Status. lean/CryoLean/Monotone.lean (added by a concurrent session while this research ran) proves the configuration side: Refines cfg cfg' -> verdict cfg e != needMoreInfo -> verdict cfg' e = verdict cfg e (verdict_refines), with accept_preserved_by_refinement, reject_preserved_by_refinement and needMoreInfo_of_refined. paper.md now states that data research 'can only resolve undecided pairs, never overturn a decided one'. Four gaps separate the theorem from that claim. (1) Experiment side: e is fixed. A user entering a missing or untrusted parameter (measurement_current and sample_resistance are null in mat_electrical_resistance_low_temperature) or confirming a profile is not covered. (2) Slot resolution happens in Python before Lean: serialize.resolve_slots picks the highest cooling_power.at_* temperature <= T_op among installed records with a known value (evidence trust is not checked) and bakes that key into the expression. Adding a documented point between T_doc and T_op therefore changes the document, and a decided NOT MET can become MET. Sourced counterexample: the Bluefors LD manual gives LD400 cooling power >= 12 uW at 20 mK, >= 400 uW at 100 mK and >= 575 uW at 120 mK; the catalog stores only the first two. For a hypothetical profile with a mandatory 500 uW heat budget at T_op = 150 mK the verdict is NOT MET today (slot 100 mK, 400 uW) and becomes MET once the documented 120 mK row is added (with a cooling_power.at_120mK vocabulary key). An untrusted higher point can also shadow a trusted lower one (an avoidable NEED INFO). (3) lookup is first-match: a duplicated key makes the verdict depend on record order; nothing enforces uniqueness (0 duplicates today in 26 configurations). (4) The 94,380 identical verdicts between 'record removed' and 'install unknown' have no theorem, and validSchedule stability under refinement is unproved.
Lean statements:
def ParamInformative (p : Param) : Prop := trustedB p.origin = true ∧ p.value.isSome
def ExpRefines (e e' : Experiment) : Prop := e'.requirements = e.requirements ∧ e'.coupled = e.coupled ∧ (e.confirmed = true → e'.confirmed = true) ∧ ∀ n p, findParam e n = some p → ParamInformative p → findParam e' n = some p
theorem verdict_refines_full (hc : Refines cfg cfg') (he : ExpRefines e e') (hd : verdict cfg e ≠ .needMoreInfo) : verdict cfg' e' = verdict cfg e
theorem verdict_eq_of_mutual_refines (h₁ : Refines cfg cfg') (h₂ : Refines cfg' cfg) : verdict cfg e = verdict cfg' e
theorem verdict_erase_uninformative (hu : (cfg.capabilities.map (·.key)).Nodup) : verdict (eraseUninformative cfg) e = verdict cfg e
theorem verdict_perm (hu : (cfg.capabilities.map (·.key)).Nodup) (hp : cfg.capabilities.Perm cfg'.capabilities) : verdict cfg e = verdict cfg' e
theorem validSchedule_refines (hr : Refines cfg cfg') (h : validSchedule cfg exps slots L = true) : validSchedule cfg' exps slots L = true
Cooling-power bracket in Lean: a new Expr node `.cooling (T : Expr)` evaluated over usable cooling_power.at_* records with Plo(T) = max{P_i : T_i <= T} and Phi(T) = min{P_j : T_j >= T}; checkLe passes on lhs <= Plo and fails on lhs > Phi, otherwise unknown. Theorems: cooling_lo_refines (Plo can only grow under Refines), cooling_hi_refines (Phi can only shrink), and cooling_bracket_sound: assuming P is non-decreasing in T (already an assumption in data/physics/coupled_models.json), Plo(T) <= P(T) <= Phi(T). The max/min over all usable points makes monotonicity a theorem that does not depend on the stored values being ordered, unlike nearest-point slots.
Proof strategy: mirror Monotone.lean. Add the param leaves (paramValue decided implies a trusted param with a value, which ExpRefines keeps) to evalCond_refines and evalExpr_refines. Mutual refinement: two applications of verdict_refines plus needMoreInfo_of_refined. eraseUninformative: Refines in both directions under Nodup, because the filter keeps the unique informative record of each key. Perm: List.find? is invariant under permutation when keys are unique. validSchedule: cooldownOf reads a usable .min record, which is informative and therefore kept, and accept_preserved_by_refinement covers the experiments. Curve: foldl max/min over a superset of points, then an order-based variant of checkLe_refines (lhs <= Plo <= Plo').
proposals.equation_latex: c \sqsubseteq c' \wedge e \sqsubseteq e' \wedge V(c,e)\neq \mathrm{NI} \Rightarrow V(c',e')=V(c,e);\qquad \underline{P}_c(T)=\max_{i:\,T_i\le T}P_i \;\le\; P(T)\;\le\; \min_{j:\,T_j\ge T}P_j=\overline{P}_c(T)
proposals.validity: Holds for data refinement only: records and parameters that cannot decide anything may be replaced or added, informative ones are kept verbatim. Edits of trusted values, profile edits, new requirements and model changes are not refinements and must keep invalidating stored results (fingerprints already do this). cooling_bracket_sound additionally assumes cooling power non-decreasing in temperature between documented points; the vendor table (20, 100, 120 mK) is consistent with it.

proposals.data_available: No new data needed: the theorems are about the existing documents. Optional data addition that exercises the slot fix: the 120 mK rows of the Bluefors LD manual (>= 360 uW LD250, >= 575 uW LD400).
proposals.expected_effect: No current verdict changes (the MXC slot is an exact 20 mK match and the Joule check is optional today), but the paper's claim becomes true for the whole pipeline: refining catalog records, user parameters or confirmations can only turn NEED INFO into a decision. The 129 decided pairs (20 MET + 109 NOT MET) then never need re-checking when data are added; only the 157 NEED INFO pairs form the re-verification set. The 94,380 identical verdicts become a corollary, order dependence disappears, and Lean-validated schedules stay valid as documentation improves. Complements the thermal workflow's TH3 (two Python-resolved slots for a FAIL-only-against-upper-bound rule): computing the bracket in Lean turns its monotonicity into a theorem. Effort S: about 150-300 lines of Lean mirroring Monotone.lean, a small curve module and a decoder check; 1 day for the theorems, 1-2 days for moving the slot into Lean.
proposals.implementation: lean/CryoLean/Monotone.lean: ParamInformative, ExpRefines, param cases of evalCond/evalExpr, verdict_refines_full, verdict_eq_of_mutual_refines, eraseUninformative + verdict_erase_uninformative, verdict_perm, validSchedule_refines. Model.lean: Expr.cooling; Checker.lean: envelope evaluation and an order-based checkLe for it; Json.lean: decode the node and reject duplicate capability keys (fail-closed). cryolean/serialize.py: emit .cooling instead of resolving $cooling to one key (keep the chosen points in the notes for display). tests/test_pipeline_extensions.py: extend test_refinement_never_changes_a_decided_verdict with parameter refinements and with added cooling points between T_doc and T_op. Audit.lean: print the axioms of the new theorems.

proposals.title: Verified multi-cycle campaign scheduling: pump-down, warm-up and sample exchange, sample thermal-exposure safety, three-valued schedule verdicts and a makespan lower-bound certificate
proposals.description:
validSchedule (Schedule.lean) accepts a slot list when every experiment is accepted, every slot starts after the documented cooldown, ends before the run length, and slots are pairwise disjoint. Checking demo D against the sources shows three gaps. (1) The CRX-VF datasheet gives a full cycle of pump down 1.5 h + station cooldown 5 h + station warmup 2 h; the model uses only the 5 h cooldown, so the earliest start is 1.5 h too early and the final warm-up is ignored. (2) There is no sample-exposure constraint. The Lean-valid demo D timeline runs Raman 5-13 h, the phase-transition POM run 13-17 h (requirement range_within 203-393 K) and then the vitrified-sample fluorescence run 17-23 h (requires <= 136 K). With all samples on the shared stage of one cooldown, as the demo's 'one cooldown' framing implies, the vitrified sample is heated above 136 K before its own measurement, and Last et al. state that devitrification occurs above about 136 K. If the samples are mounted separately, the CRX-VF needs a full 8.5 h cycle per exchange, which the schedule does not contain. (3) No setup or temperature-transition times, and no rule for one-sided time specs: '< 2 hours' (TeslatronPT sample cooldown) is a sound upper bound for scheduling, while the Bluefors fast-sample-exchange page gives 'typically less than 7 hours' in its prose and a guaranteed '< 7 hours' in its table, with the note that the cooldown time 'is for a typical configuration'; using it needs M4's reviewed promise annotation. Lean also proves validity, not optimality.
Lean statements (sketch):
structure Slot2 where exp sample : String; start dur tLo tHi : Q
structure Cycle where start : Q; samples : List String; slots : List Slot2
def cycleTimesOf (cfg) : Option (Q × Q × Q)  -- pump, cool, warm, read only from usable records (pumpdown_time.max, cooldown_time.max, warmup_time.max)
inductive SchedVerdict | valid | invalid | needMoreInfo
def CampaignOK cfg exps (camp : List Cycle) (L : Q) : Prop := (∀ e ∈ exps, verdict cfg e = .accept) ∧ (∀ c ∈ camp, ∀ s ∈ c.slots, c.start + pump + cool ≤ s.start) ∧ SlotChain (fun a b => a.start + a.dur + τ a b ≤ b.start) ∧ (lastStop cᵢ + warm ≤ cᵢ₊₁.start) ∧ (lastStop + warm ≤ L) ∧ (∀ c, ∀ m ∈ c.samples, ∀ s ∈ c.slots, s.start < done m c → s.tHi ≤ maxExposure m ∧ minExposure m ≤ s.tLo) ∧ (∀ s ∈ c.slots, s.sample ∈ c.samples)
theorem validCampaign_valid_iff : validCampaign cfg exps camp L = .valid ↔ CampaignOK cfg exps camp L
theorem validCampaign_nmi : (a needed time is undocumented, untrusted or only 'typical') → validCampaign … = .needMoreInfo
theorem campaign_exposure_safe : CampaignOK … → no mounted sample is taken outside its declared exposure window before its own last slot ends
theorem campaign_makespan_lb : CampaignOK … → lastStop camp ≥ camp.length * (pump + cool + warm) + Σ dur  (warm counted once per cycle)
theorem validCampaign_refines : Refines cfg cfg' → validCampaign cfg … = .valid → validCampaign cfg' … = .valid  (uses M1)
Optimality: Z3 returns its optimum; Lean certifies it when lastStop equals the lower bound (single cycle with documented zero or summed minimal transitions), otherwise a compiled exhaustive check over orders for n <= 8 with a generic soundness theorem; never a kernel enumeration. Proof strategy: Boolean checker and Prop spec side by side, as validSchedule_sound/complete do now; exposure safety by induction on the slot chain; the lower bound by summing the chain inequalities (linear arithmetic over Q or core Rat).
proposals.equation_latex: t_{\mathrm{pump}}+t_{\mathrm{cool}}\le s_1,\quad s_i+d_i+\tau(T_i,T_{i+1})\le s_{i+1},\quad s_n+d_n+t_{\mathrm{warm}}\le L,\quad \forall m,\ \forall i<\mathrm{done}(m):\ T^{\max}_i\le T^{\exp}_m;\qquad C_{\max}\ge k\,(t_{\mathrm{pump}}+t_{\mathrm{cool}}+t_{\mathrm{warm}})+\textstyle\sum_i d_i
proposals.validity: Exposure limits are only as complete as the profiles declare them (a new sourced field per profile; the vitrified profile already cites the 136 K threshold). Times are taken only from trusted records; upper-bound wording ('<', 'less than') is accepted for durations, 'typical'/'approx.' wording is not. Single-cycle optimality certificates assume transitions are documented or bounded below; multi-cycle optimality is certified only for small instances.

The exposure-safe single-cycle order is vitrified fluorescence (<= 136 K) -> Raman (133.15 K) -> POM (203-393 K), with makespan >= 1.5 + 5 + 18 = 24.5 h, or 26.5 h if the run must end warm, instead of 23 h; the E6 sweep threshold moves from 23 h to at least 24.5 h. Because the CRX-VF documents no ramp rates, the honest schedule verdict is NEED INFO until a ramp rate is entered. Separate mounting needs 3 cycles: 3 x 8.5 h + 18 h = 43.5 h. When transitions are zero or documented, the Lean lower bound certifies Z3's single-cycle optimum. Effort M-L: about 400-700 lines of Lean, about 200 lines of Z3 encoding with sequence-dependent setups, three vocabulary keys and one profile field.

proposals.title: Verified three-valued explanations: refinement-stable rejection certificates, certified minimal sufficient fact sets (abductive explanations) computed with the Lean checker as oracle, contrastive explanations, and 'what to document next' plans for NEED INFO
proposals.description:
Today 'why' comes from Z3 unsat cores, which the paper itself calls advisory and 'not itself evidence'. NEED INFO pairs (157 of 286) list undecided items, and completeness.py splits gaps into configuration-side and experiment-side, but nothing certifies that an explanation is sufficient or minimal, or says which single documentation would decide the most pairs. Because verdict_refines makes the verdict monotone in information, one Lean evaluation on a restricted configuration certifies sufficiency for every completion.
Lean statements:
def restrictTo (S : List String) (cfg : Configuration) : Configuration := { cfg with capabilities := cfg.capabilities.filter (·.key ∈ S) }
theorem restrictTo_refines (hS : ∀ k ∈ S, lookup cfg' k = lookup cfg k) : Refines (restrictTo S cfg) cfg'
theorem axp_sufficient (hS : ∀ k ∈ S, lookup cfg' k = lookup cfg k) (hv : verdict (restrictTo S cfg) e = v) (hd : v ≠ .needMoreInfo) : verdict cfg' e = v
theorem axp_not_sufficient (hv : verdict (restrictTo (S.erase s) cfg) e ≠ v) : ¬ Sufficient (S.erase s) cfg e v  -- the restricted configuration itself is the counter-witness
inductive ItemRef | req (i : Nat) | coupled (i : Nat)
def checkRejectCert (cfg) (e) (i : ItemRef) : Bool  -- e.confirmed ∧ item i is mandatory, applicable and its outcome is .fail
theorem checkRejectCert_sound : checkRejectCert cfg e i = true → RejectSpec cfg e
theorem checkRejectCert_complete : verdict cfg e = .reject → ∃ i, checkRejectCert cfg e i = true
theorem checkRejectCert_refines : Refines cfg cfg' → checkRejectCert cfg e i = true → checkRejectCert cfg' e i = true
theorem item_local : (∀ k ∈ factsOf e i, lookup cfg' k = lookup cfg k) → itemOutcome cfg' e i = itemOutcome cfg e i
theorem possibly (hr : Refines cfg w) (hv : verdict w e = v) : ∃ cfg', Refines cfg cfg' ∧ verdict cfg' e = v
Method. (a) Abductive explanation (AXp) of a decided verdict v: start from all keys read by mandatory applicable items and drop keys one at a time while verdict (restrictTo S cfg) e = v (Ignatiev et al.'s deletion algorithm, a linear number of oracle calls). The oracle is the verified checker, so sufficiency for all completions follows from axp_sufficient and subset-minimality from the |S| failed deletions. With a monotone verdict every such explanation is automatically robust to later disclosure, the property that fails for defeasible classifiers (Li 2026). (b) Contrastive explanations (CXp) by minimal-hitting-set duality: for a NOT MET pair with two violated items, any change that stops the rejection must touch both items; Lean re-checks each proposed CXp. (c) NEED INFO: undecided items, their missing facts and witnesses. A hypothetical completion w that refines cfg and gives MET (or NOT MET) proves the verdict is still reachable (Bruns-Godefroid generalized model checking: does some completion satisfy it). Witnesses are never stored as evidence. Facts are ranked by the number of pairs they can decide, a deterministic analogue of de Kleer and Williams's next-measurement selection. The thorough semantics (NEED INFO iff two completions disagree) is not required; witnesses are sound in one direction only.
proposals.equation_latex: \mathrm{AXp}(S):\iff V(c|_S,e)=v\neq\mathrm{NI}\ \wedge\ \forall s\in S.\ V(c|_{S\setminus\{s\}},e)\neq v;\qquad c|_S\sqsubseteq c'\ \Rightarrow\ V(c',e)=v;\qquad \mathrm{CXp}=\mathrm{MHS}(\{\mathrm{AXp}\})
proposals.validity: Sufficiency is relative to the fixed requirement and model set and to configuration-side facts; parameter facts need M1's ExpRefines. AXps are not unique (the deletion order chooses one; cost-based orders are possible). Possibility witnesses use synthetic records and only show that a verdict is reachable, never that it is likely.

proposals.data_available: Everything needed is in the repository: per-item outcomes and per-key records in the check-batch output, verdict_refines in lean/CryoLean/Monotone.lean, completeness.py's gap classification. No new data.
proposals.expected_effect: From a read-only re-run of the compiled checker on all 286 pairs (counts reproduced exactly): 85 NOT MET pairs have exactly one violated item and 24 have two, so all 109 get a one-item Lean certificate that provably survives any future documentation, and the 24 two-item pairs get CXps that must touch both items. The 20 MET pairs need one passing fact per mandatory item (3 items in 16 pairs, 4 in 4). The 157 NEED INFO pairs contain 466 undecided items (no item is permanently unsupported, so catalog records or user parameters can still decide every one of them); 19 are one passing item away from MET; 156 can be decided NOT MET by documenting a single failing fact. Top single facts by NEED INFO pairs touched: temperature.range of lakeshore_ccs_400h (an inferred estimate today) and of the three Leica CM1950 configurations (7 pairs each), and of linkam_thms600_heating_only (6). Z3 cores remain proposals; the user-facing 'why' becomes Lean-checked. Effort M: about 300-500 lines of Lean (certificate checkers reuse the Soundness lemmas) and about 200 lines of Python on top of completeness.py.
proposals.implementation: New lean/CryoLean/Certify.lean: restrictTo and its lemmas, ItemRef, checkRejectCert, checkAcceptCert (a witness key or failing condition per mandatory item) with soundness, completeness and refinement stability; Main.lean entry points check-cert and check-restricted (batch). cryolean/explain.py: deletion-based AXp over lean_runner.check_batch, CXp by minimal hitting sets over violated items, NEED INFO plans (undecided items, missing facts, optimistic and pessimistic completions verified by Lean, greedy ranking of (configuration, key) facts by pairs decided). The bridge shows certificates in the verdict card. Tests: on random subsets S, a decided restricted verdict equals the full verdict.

proposals.title: Bound polarity and physical-world (certain-answer) soundness: one-sided datasheet bounds ('<4 K', '< -195 °C', '≥ 12 µW') may justify PASS but never FAIL, with first-class necessary/sufficient coupled relations
proposals.description:
Spec.lean reads every trusted number as the exact capability, so RejectSpec means 'violated by the documented number'. Datasheets state one-sided promises: Lake Shore CCS-100 '<4 K to 325 K', Linkam THMS600 '< -195°C to 600°C', the Bluefors LD manual 'Cooling power at 20 mK: ≥ 12 µW' (LD400), and Bluefors now publishes cooling power only as a guaranteed '>' value. A promise 'reaches below 4 K' supports PASS for any requirement at or above 4 K but says nothing about 2 K, yet the checker rejects 2 K requirements on these stages. Proposal: give every numeric end a promise in {exact, achievable, limit, typical}. achievable(q) means the true capability is at least as good as q (supports PASS); limit(q) means it is no better than q (supports FAIL); exact gives both; typical gives neither. Each requirement gets a level in {physical, guarantee}; at guarantee level the printed number is treated as the contract value, which is today's behaviour. Coupled models get first-class necessary relations (fail-only) and sufficient relations (pass-only), replacing the validity-list encoding that sibling proposals TH3, TH4, MAG-1 and MAG-4 use for the same pattern.
Lean statements:
inductive Promise | exact | achievable | limit | typical
structure End where q : Quantity; promise : Promise   -- CapValue.range (lo hi : End) | .max (m : End) | .min (m : End) | …
inductive Level | physical | guarantee
def Consistent (w : World) (cfg : Configuration) : Prop  -- w assigns true values allowed by every trusted promise
def checkValueP (lvl : Level) : Constraint → CapValueP → Outcome  -- PASS only via achievable/exact ends, FAIL only via limit/exact ends
theorem checkValueP_pass_sound : checkValueP .physical k v = .pass → ∀ t, Allows v t → ValueMeetsTrue k t
theorem checkValueP_fail_sound : checkValueP .physical k v = .fail → ∀ t, Allows v t → ValueFailsTrue k t
theorem checkValueP_exact : checkValueP lvl k (allExact v) = checkValue k v  -- conservative extension: today's theorems are the special case
theorem verdictP_accept_sound : verdictP cfg e = .accept → ∀ w, Consistent w cfg → AcceptSpecW w e
theorem verdictP_reject_sound : verdictP cfg e = .reject → ∀ w, Consistent w cfg → RejectSpecW w e
theorem coupled_roles : necessary relations never PASS an item and sufficient relations never FAIL one
theorem verdictP_refines : sharpening a promise (typical → achievable → exact) or adding a limit is a Refines step (with M1)
Proof strategy: per constraint shape (11 shapes x pass/fail), unfold Allows and use transitivity of Q.le (or core Rat with grind); verdict level by reusing the outcomes/accept_iff_outcomes structure of Soundness.lean with the world-indexed specification; conservativity by rfl-style case analysis when every end is exact.
proposals.equation_latex: \mathrm{PASS}\Rightarrow\forall w\models c:\ \mathrm{Meets}(k,w(\kappa)),\qquad \mathrm{FAIL}\Rightarrow\forall w\models c:\ \mathrm{Fails}(k,w(\kappa)),\qquad w\models(q,\mathrm{achievable})\iff w(\kappa)\succeq q,\quad w\models(q,\mathrm{limit})\iff w(\kappa)\preceq q
proposals.validity: Physical-level soundness is relative to correct promise annotation, which is a reviewed reading of the source wording and not something Lean can check. Guarantee-level requirements keep today's semantics and must say so in the verdict text. Hard limits must come from sources: vendor minima or reference data with the assumption stated.

proposals.title: Capability dominance and certified parameter thresholds: better hardware never breaks a MET, and exact repair thresholds certified by one Lean evaluation
proposals.description:
Prove that the requirement language is monotone in the 'better' direction of each vocabulary key, and that coupled expressions are monotone in each leaf whose polarity is syntactically known.
Lean statements:
def BetterFor : Constraint → CapValue → CapValue → Prop  -- higher .max, lower .min, wider .range, larger .count, superset .set; flags, enums and countEquals: equality only
theorem checkValue_better_pass : BetterFor k v v' → checkValue k v = .pass → checkValue k v' = .pass
theorem checkValue_better_fail : BetterFor k v v' → checkValue k v' = .fail → checkValue k v = .fail
inductive Pol | up | down | none
def Expr.pol (leaf) : Expr → Pol  -- add keeps, sub/neg flip, mul keeps only when both factors are provably >= 0 from the validity list
theorem evalExpr_mono_leaf : x.pol leaf = .up → value ≤ value' → evalExpr (… value) ≤ evalExpr (… value')
theorem verdict_dominance : Dominates e cfg cfg' → verdict cfg e = .accept → verdict cfg' e = .accept
theorem param_down_keeps_accept : lhs.pol p = .up → rhs.pol p = .none → verdict (e.set p a) = .accept → 0 ≤ b → b ≤ a → verdict (e.set p b) = .accept
theorem affine_threshold : lhs = a + b·p syntactically, 0 < b, a + b·p* = rhs → (outcome = .pass ↔ p ≤ p*)
Expr has no division, so Z3 or Python proposes p* as an exact rational and Lean checks a + b·p* = rhs with one multiplication, a certifying-algorithm step. The non-negativity side conditions already exist: serialize.coupled_docs adds 0 <= param validity bounds for every parameter not marked signed. Proof automation: core Lean 4.35 Rat has grind ordered-ring instances, so the order lemmas need no Mathlib (or prove them once for the custom Q).
proposals.validity: Only for constraints with an order (flags, enumerations, countEquals and 'must be absent' are excluded) and leaves with a known sign; signed parameters (thermal-contraction strains) get Pol.none and no claim. Dominance is relative to one experiment's requirement set.

proposals.title: Tolerance-interval verdicts: exact rational interval arithmetic with an inclusion theorem, robust MET/NOT MET at a stated tolerance, conservative extension, and inflated explanations
proposals.description:
Measured inputs carry uncertainties (Krinner et al.'s per-line loads 0.013(6), 0.029(5), 0.020(16) and 0.050(3) µW; Leica ±3 K and ±5 K), but the model evaluates central values only ('measurement uncertainties of the per-line loads are not propagated', coupled_models.json). Stage 1 (needs M5): for expressions monotone in every uncertain leaf, the exact range is two corner evaluations of the existing checker (all leaves at their unfavourable ends, then all at their favourable ends), justified by evalExpr_mono_leaf. Stage 2: general interval evaluation.
Lean statements:
structure IQ where lo hi : Rat   -- or the custom Q; lo ≤ hi checked by the decoder
def IQ.add/sub/neg; def IQ.mul (x y : IQ) : IQ := ⟨min4 (x.lo*y.lo) (x.lo*y.hi) (x.hi*y.lo) (x.hi*y.hi), max4 …⟩  -- four-corner rule; Mathlib's NonemptyInterval product does not apply to ℚ
theorem IQ.mul_mem : a ∈ x → b ∈ y → a * b ∈ x.mul y   -- inclusion (containment) property
theorem evalExprI_sound : Consistent w cfg → evalExprI cfg e x = .ok I → Denotes_w x q → q ∈ I
def checkLeI (a b : IQ) : Outcome := if a.hi ≤ b.lo then .pass else if b.hi < a.lo then .fail else .unknown  -- 'borderline'
theorem verdictI_accept_sound / verdictI_reject_sound : ∀ worlds within the stated tolerances
theorem verdictI_point : all intervals degenerate → verdictI cfg e = verdict cfg e   -- conservative extension
theorem verdictI_narrow : tolerances only shrink → InfoLe (verdictI wide) (verdictI narrow)   -- tightening tolerances is a refinement (M1)
Inflated explanations (Izza et al.): for a MET pair, report for each fact the widest interval on which MET still holds, for example the cooling power below which a repair stops passing. Decision procedure: as now, the compiled checker runs and generic theorems justify it, or decide +kernel; never native_decide (LeanCert's native mode adds an auxiliary axiom per call, which the Gatekeeper forbids).
proposals.validity: Robustness is relative to the stated tolerance. Statistical 1σ error bars are not hard bounds, so verdicts must be labelled 'robust at kσ'. Interval evaluation is exact for single-use monotone expressions such as the MXC budget; repeated variables overestimate (the dependency effect), which can only add NEED INFO, never an unsound verdict.

proposals.risks: Turning a headline NOT MET into 'borderline' must be communicated carefully; choosing k is a policy decision; one-sided promises (M4) give infinite interval ends that need special cases in products; a migration from custom Q to core Rat touches every proof file.

rejected_ideas: Re-proving configuration-side information monotonicity: a concurrent session added lean/CryoLean/Monotone.lean (verdict_refines, accept/reject_preserved_by_refinement, needMoreInfo_of_refined) during this research; M1 extends it rather than duplicating it.

A Belnap four-valued verdict for conflicting trusted sources: the 26 configurations contain 0 duplicate capability keys, so enforcing key uniqueness at decode time plus an order-invariance theorem (M1) is cheaper and closes the same hole.

Thorough (completion-exact) NEED INFO semantics, where NEED INFO holds exactly when two completions disagree: deciding it quantifies over all completions (minimal robust cores are Sigma2p-complete in the closely related disclosure setting); the compositional semantics is sound, and M3 offers one-directional witness checks instead.

Bayesian or entropy-based measurement selection (de Kleer and Williams) inside the trusted core: it needs priors over undocumented vendor specifications, which would turn NEED INFO into guesses; M3 keeps a deterministic decisiveness ranking, and entropy could only be an advisory layer.

LeanCert or native_decide for interval checks: native evaluation adds one auxiliary axiom per call (Wang et al. 2026), which violates the Gatekeeper's standard-axioms rule; exact rationals with generic theorems, or decide +kernel, are used instead.

Mathlib's NonemptyInterval as the interval type: its multiplication 'does not apply to ℚ or ℝ' because it assumes monotone multiplication, and CryoLean has signed products (eps_sample - eps_holder); the four-corner rule is needed (M6).
Floating-point intervals (FloatLib, Flean): exact rationals already decide a pair in 0.14 s median including process start, and floats would add rounding obligations without benefit.

Reconstructing Z3 proofs inside Lean (lean-smt or SMTCoq style): verdicts are recomputed by the verified checker, so small certificate checkers (M2, M3, M5) give the same assurance with a smaller trusted base.

Signal-temporal-logic robustness degrees as verdicts: CryoLean's constraints are static inequalities whose exact margins are already computed; robustness to tolerances is handled by interval semantics (M6).
Kernel decide over all schedule permutations as an optimality proof beyond about 8 experiments: factorial growth; M2 uses lower-bound certificates and a compiled exhaustive check only for small n.
Migrating the trusted core to Mathlib's ℚ: it would enlarge the build and the trusted base; core Lean 4.35 already ships Rat with grind ordered-ring instances.
Researching QuickXplain or minimal-correction-set algorithms for explanations: the parallel workflow covers them; M3 only adds the Lean certificate layer that makes any such output checkable.
